newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds climb on overseas bids and U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds climb on overseas bids and U.S. data.

text.p: Irish government bonds held onto sharp morning gains in steady trade on Friday afternoon as the market continued to be boosted by bond-friendly U.S. data and good overseas bidding, dealers said.
"Dublin has had a "catch-up day' after a fairly uninspiring week. The long-end has seen most of the buying today which has come from overseas investors," one dealer said.

By 1534 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 had risen 35p from Thursday's close to 101.80 to yield 5.97 percent while the eight percent bond due 2006 had risen 48p from the close to 108.68 to yield 6.64 percent.
Earlier, UK gilts secured new higher ground after U.S. data showed a surprise 0.5 percent fall in industrial output in October against expectations of a modest rise.
Dealers said more short-term covering in gilts could push the market higher before the close.
Dealers in Dublin reiterated that one of the major issues affecting bond markets in coming weeks would be Germany's key role in negotiations on the EMU stability pact.

"Germany has a key bargaining position and we're getting conflicting statements every day from Bundesbank Council members. I think the whole EMU process will go right up to the wire and will keep bond markets on tenterhooks," a dealer said.
Dealers said next week's UK data, including money supply, GDP and industrial production, would provide the main focus for the Irish bond market.
